validity.researcher_notes: WIKI-CITATION TRAP CONFIRMED AS EXPECTED: wiki_citations.json for this page returns 27 footnotes, and every one of them is about the international Bukhara-Tashkent-Bishkek-Almaty (BTBA/БГР-ТБА) trunk as a whole system, or about downstream Kyrgyz/Kazakh sections (KazTransGaz, Intergas Central Asia, Kyrgyzstan launch ceremonies) -- none is a dedicated technical source for the 'Mubarek-Zirabulak II' string specifically. So I engaged the sheet's OWN two currently-cited sources (kun.uz 2020-12-26 and uzreport.news 2020-09-09, both 'EPSILON (EDC)' progress releases on Uzbek gas-infrastructure modernization) directly, verified live, and read them in full rather than trusting the wiki footnote list. EXISTENCE: CONFIRMED, independent of GEM/gem.wiki. kun.uz verbatim: 'В круглосуточном режиме продолжаются работы на других участках магистральных газопроводов «Мубарек - Зирабулак» (БГР-ТБА)' -- note the PLURAL 'gazoprovodov' ('pipelines', not 'pipeline'), i.e. the source itself treats Mubarek-Zirabulak as more than one physical line, consistent with GEM's I/II/III split. uzreport.news is more specific still and itemizes discrete capital-repair (капремонт) projects by управление (Zirabulakskoe UMG), by km range, and by completion deadline: 'Зирабулакское УМГ, капремонт МГ «Мубарек-Зирабулак» (БГР-ТБА) I, II, III нитки, участок 50-78 км (Ø1020х5x12 мм - 2,1 км). Срок завершения до 01.12.2020 г.' and 'Капремонт МГ «Мубарек-Зирабулак» I, II нитки, участок 3-50 км (Ø1020х12 мм - 8,0 км). Срок завершения до 01.10.2020 г.'. This is a genuine engineering/works document (specific km markers, specific deadlines), not vague PR, and it explicitly names 'II' among the strings under active capital repair in 2020 -- so the pipe existed, in service, and was being maintained as of that date. CLASSIFICATION: correct as recorded -- transmission trunk, gas fuel, matches the source's 'magistral'nyy gazoprovod' language. DUPLICATE CHECK vs roster (P6933/P6935, same corridor): NOT a duplicate/double-count. Per the standing rule that only sourcing decides duplication (the Kazakhstan cluster-A lesson), I looked for any source that describes I/II/III as one pipe under different names -- found none; instead uzreport.news affirmatively treats them as parallel, separately-tracked strings ('I, II нитки' vs 'I, II, III нитки' get DIFFERENT km-range repair scopes, i.e. they are physically distinguishable pipes with different maintenance histories, not one pipe recorded three times). Keep P6934 as its own row. SPEC (the flagged concern): GEM records Diameter=1021mm for P6934, sourced to this same uzreport.news URL. But the source itself states 'I, II, III нитки ... Ø1020х12 мм' and 'I, II нитки ... Ø1020х12 мм' -- i.e. it gives ONE diameter, 1020mm (outer, 12mm wall), covering the group that includes string II. GEM's own automated ref-checker already flagged this before I started (existing_ref_checks: '200 but data value not found (none of ["1,021", "1021"])'). Cross-checking the sibling rows makes the pattern unmistakable: P6933 (string I) = 1020mm and its OWN citation matches; P6935 (string III) = 1022mm; P6934 (string II) = 1021mm. Three parallel strings differing by exactly +1mm in strict index order (I=1020, II=1021, III=1022) is not a plausible engineering fact for Soviet-standard pipe (GOST large-diameter pipe comes in fixed sizes -- 720/820/1020/1220mm, never 1mm increments), and it has the clean signature of a segment-index value bleeding into the diameter cell. This is exactly the pattern the task brief hypothesized -- and here it is independently confirmed BOTH by the general implausibility argument AND by a live, on-point primary source (the row's own existing citation) that gives a single, specific 1020mm figure for the group spanning this exact string. Recommend correcting Diameter to 1020mm. Tier is medium, not high: uzreport.news is the only source I found that states a number, and though kun.uz (different outlet, later date) independently corroborates existence/ongoing-repair, it does not restate the diameter, so I do not have two independent sources agreeing on the numeric value itself -- both diameter-bearing traces run through the single EPSILON EDC 2020 works-progress report. ATTRIBUTION: StartLocation=Mubarek/EndLocation=Zirabulak (both Uzbekistan) is directly confirmed by both sources' pipeline name and by kun.uz's explicit 'Mubarek - Zirabulak' phrasing. Owner=Uztransgaz (100%) is highly plausible -- the repair works are attributed to 'Zirabulakskoe UMG' (Управление Магистральных Газопроводов), and an independent web search confirms a live 'Zirabulakskoe UMG' branch office (contact email umg_zirabulak@utg.uz) under Uztransgaz's own utg.uz domain -- but I could not get this to a citable standard within url_verifier (see fills: UNRESOLVED for both Owner and Operator refs).

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Newest segment-specific dated evidence is Dec 2020 (kun.uz), describing active round-the-clock capital-repair/modernization work on the Mubarek-Zirabulak strings (including string II explicitly per uzreport.news' 'I, II нитки' repair item), with throughput expected to rise from 67 to 72 mcm/day on completion -- unambiguous evidence of an in-service, actively-maintained trunk, not a dormant or proposed one, so the dormancy-inference ladder (2y->shelved / 4y->cancelled) does not apply here at all: that ladder is for proposed/shelved projects going quiet, not for a Soviet-era operating trunk between capital-repair cycles. I also searched specifically for anything newer (2021-2026) naming this segment and found nothing segment-specific, but did find strong general-corridor context that the wider Bukhara-Tashkent-Bishkek-Almaty / Central-Asian transit network remains a live, actively-expanding system through 2026 (e.g. gazeta.uz 2026-06-10 on Kazakhstan/Gazprom increasing gas transit through this same corridor system to Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan under a 2025-2040 contract) -- this is corridor-level, not string-II-specific, so I am not using it as a citation for this row, but it weighs against any dormancy reading. Confirm as-is; no change proposed.
